domain.name: fnv
domain.one_line: Sequential ordering under a martingale (MMFE) demand signal: place N orders while demand information is progressively revealed, realize demand at the horizon, and sell against cumulative inventory to maximize expected profit.

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current ordering period n (1-indexed, 1..N); the horizon ends after the order at period N

state_variables.name: inventory
state_variables.desc: cumulative quantity ordered so far (sum of past decisions); non-decreasing, sold against realized demand at the horizon

state_variables.name: information
state_variables.desc: I[period]: cumulative demand-signal information revealed so far (the MMFE martingale); observed by the agent before each order

state_variables.name: total_cost
state_variables.desc: sum of ordering costs incurred so far; subtracted from terminal revenue to give profit

info_fields.name: cost
info_fields.desc: ordering cost incurred this period = (c1 + (period-1)*lamb) * order

info_fields.name: demand
info_fields.desc: realized demand at the horizon: mu + information (mmfe_mode='additive') or exp(mu + information) (mmfe_mode='multiplicative'); 0 until the terminal period

info_fields.name: sales
info_fields.desc: units sold at the horizon = min(demand, inventory); 0 until the terminal period

decisions.name: order

type.rationale: order quantities are continuous non-negative reals in the MMFE ordering problem

bounds.rationale: additive MMFE with mu=1 and stdev<=0.3: mean demand ~ 1, so an upper bound of ~3 (mu + several stdevs, spread over N orders) covers the useful action scale

decisions.desc: quantity ordered this period; adds to cumulative inventory. Consumed by the _mdp layer; the gym action_modes are agent-facing encodings.

updates: demand = (mu + information) if mmfe_mode == 'additive' else exp(mu + information)

per_step_components.name: ordering
per_step_components.desc: per-step ordering cost as a (negative) profit contribution

per_step_components.name: revenue
per_step_components.desc: terminal sales revenue r*min(demand, inventory); 0 until the horizon (sales==0). Episode total = -total_cost + revenue = profit.

constants.name: N
constants.desc: number of ordering periods (= horizon T); paper default 3

constants.name: stdev
constants.desc: total demand std dev; the per-period signal schedule signal_stdevs is derived from it and the epoch spacing

constants.name: t_last
constants.desc: time location of the last ordering epoch (paper T, in (0,1)); renamed from T to avoid the reserved horizon symbol. Sets the epoch spacing tau and thus signal_stdevs.

constants.name: lamb
constants.desc: ordering-cost increment per period: rate at period n is c1 + (n-1)*lamb

constants.name: c1
constants.desc: ordering cost per unit in period 1 (paper default 1.0)

constants.name: mu
constants.desc: additive MMFE: mean demand (E[D] = mu + I, E[I]=0)

constants.name: mmfe_mode
constants.desc: MMFE link selector (categorical): 'additive' -> D = mu + I, 'multiplicative' -> D = exp(mu + I). Selects the terminal link ONLY (the demand-signal family is the same normal-increment MMFE either way) — a constant-conditioned dynamics expression, not an uncertainty candidate. The base scenario is 'additive'; the 'mmmfe' instance selects 'multiplicative' (and, independently, widens stdev to 0.2). Read by the R-event demand update and passed straight through to FnvScenario.mmfe_mode by the adapter.

constants.name: signal_stdevs
constants.desc: DERIVED, pre-resolved per-period signal volatility (length N+1): signal_stdevs[n] = sqrt(tau[n+1]-tau[n]) * stdev, tau = concat([0], linspace(0, t_last, N), [1]). Baked as exact float reprs so the interpreter's normal draw matches the domain's bit-for-bit; the domain re-derives it from stdev/t_last/N (see assumptions_log).

ammfe.desc: mean-zero MMFE increment revealed at period n; std = signal_stdevs[n], the pre-resolved per-period volatility schedule (see assumptions_log). Observed, not latent — it enters `information`.

action_modes.name: order
action_modes.desc: identity: the agent sets the order quantity directly, clipped to the non-negative box.

reward_modes.name: profit
reward_modes.desc: per-step objective.total = ordering + revenue = -cost each period, plus terminal sales revenue (sense=maximize, no sign flip). Episode sum = profit.

requires_memory.rationale: fully observed: the MMFE signal is revealed into `information`, so (inventory, information, period) is the sufficient statistic; no hidden latent

obs_normalization.rationale: inventory, information, and orders_to_go sit on modestly heterogeneous scales; spec §8.3 says normalize

assumptions_log: MMFE INFORMATION PROCESS: demand information arrives as a martingale (Heath & Jackson 1994 MMFE). The increment revealed at period n is mean-zero normal with std signal_stdevs[n]; cumulative information I[period] is observed before each order, and demand realizes at the horizon as D = mu + I (additive) or D = exp(mu + I) (multiplicative), selected by the categorical `mmfe_mode` constant.

DERIVED SCHEDULE BAKED AS DATA: signal_stdevs[n] = sqrt(tau[n+1]-tau[n]) * stdev with tau = concat([0], linspace(0, t_last, N), [1]) is scenario construction (domain-side). The IR carries the *resolved* schedule as exact float reprs so the interpreter's normal draw matches the domain's FnvScenario.signal bit-for-bit; instances that change stdev/t_last/N would need a re-resolved schedule (FNV's parameter variety lives in the design grids, exercised by conformance, not this differential).

1-INDEXED HORIZON: the N=3 ordering periods run on a 1-indexed clock (1..N); the interpreter terminates when the post-increment clock reaches horizon.T, so the terminal clock value is N+1 = 4 (horizon.T = 4, not N). The demand-signal seed key uses period directly (1..N), matching the domain's state.period, so trajectories diff bit-exactly under seed scheme v2 ([period, source_id, 1, episode_seed, seed_salt]).

TERMINAL REALIZATION: demand and sales are realized under the `period == N` guard (event R), before the period increment; they are 0 on every non-terminal row. Objective total = -cost + revenue accumulates to profit = revenue - total_cost.

MMFE LINK IS A CONSTANT SELECTION: additive (D = mu + I) and multiplicative (D = exp(mu + I)) use the same demand-signal family (the `signal` slot's generator is identical); they diverge only in the deterministic terminal link, applied once at the horizon in the R event. That link is not an uncertainty candidate but a constant-conditioned dynamics expression, keyed on the categorical `mmfe_mode` constant ('additive' | 'multiplicative'). The base scenario is 'additive'; the 'mmmfe' instance selects 'multiplicative' AND independently widens the signal (stdev 0.1 -> 0.2, with the derived signal_stdevs schedule re-baked to match) — showing both a mode selector and a derived-constant re-bake under one instance override. Both are differentially verified by the covering-set sweep (--all-instances): base = aMMFE, instance mmmfe = mMMFE.

DESIGN GRIDS (PARAMETER SWEEPS) OUT OF IR SCOPE: the mode is now in-IR (the `additive` selector), but the aMMFE / mMMFE parameter sweeps (stdev x t_last x lamb ranges) remain experiment-design grids (spec §5.6), consumed only by training/eval drivers. The IR formalizes concrete scenarios (base + instances); grid coverage is verified structurally by the conformance harness.
